title: Withdraw: a poke starts a wave along a horseshoe of relay cells

trials.label: poked at the top: the wave goes both ways, the left arm ends first
poked on the right (only type-1 cells hit): the lower arm ends first
poked on the left, at the gap: two fronts meet on the right
poked at the bottom, near one end: the wave goes one way

mechanism: The 10 type-2 cells grow into a horseshoe: a ring around the middle of the body with a gap on the lower left, with the 38 type-1 cells filling the space around it. While the body waits, each ring cell slowly charges up to 80-90% of the way to firing (never all the way on its own), so one spike from a ring neighbour fires it, and so does the small nudge from a poked type-1 cell beside it; type-1 cells ignore each other, so they never pass a signal on themselves. From the first ring cell to fire, a wave runs along the ring one cell per tick, both ways if it starts partway along and one way if it starts at an end. A ring cell that has just fired ignores everything for the next few ticks, so the spike coming back from the cell ahead does nothing: the wave only moves forward, and stops when it runs off an end of the horseshoe. The response is scored over three ticks starting 4 ticks after the poke (the quiet wait before the poke counts too, and nothing fires then), and by that time the front on the shorter arm has usually run off its end, so the one front still going is on the longer arm, on the far side. A poke right at the gap sets off both ends at once, and the two fronts run toward each other and meet on the far side. Placement matters because the wave can only travel along ring cells that touch: scatter the same cells at random and the ring breaks into islands, so the wave has nowhere to go.
evidence:
All numbers are from the 48 held-out trials (new directions and distances) that the exporter also uses.
- Score 0.81. Messages off: 0.00.
- What the wave does in those 48 trials. In 26 it goes both ways, but the short arm's front runs off its end before scoring. In 15 it starts at an end and goes one way. In 4 (pokes at the gap) two fronts meet on the far side while scoring is on, and in 1 more both fronts are still running. In 2 no wave starts. So in 41 of 48 only one front is firing while the response is scored. One-way trials average 0.81 and two-way trials 0.86.
- Every spike in the scored response ticks is on the far half of the body (2 trials have none). No cell fires before the poke, and no cell fires more than once in a trial.
- Types shuffled into random places: about 0.03 on average over 200 shuffles. Most random arrangements score 0, 12% score above 0.1, and the luckiest scored 0.50. The exporter's own 8 shuffles give -0.007. A shuffled ring breaks into islands of at most 6 cells.
- All cells made type 2: 0.61. All made type 1: 0.00.
- Removing one ring cell costs 0.09 to 0.68 for 8 of the 10, because it cuts the path. The costliest (0.68) is on the right-hand side of the ring, just above the middle. The two extra cells at the lower end cost 0.01 or less, and no type-1 cell costs more than 0.02.
- Ring cells' rest after firing cut from 3 ticks to 2: 0.81, unchanged. To 1 tick: 0.40. To 0: -0.02, and the ring re-fires over and over. Letting ring cells restart 50% to 90% of the way to firing after their rest, instead of from empty: 0.81, unchanged. So the rest alone is what stops the wave bouncing back.
- Ring cells with no slow charge-up, or that lose half their charge every tick: 0.00.
- Ring cells' charge when a poke can arrive: 80% of the way to firing at tick 11, 90% at tick 16. A ring neighbour's spike is enough from about 29% up, and a type-1 nudge from about 71% up.
- Ring cells deaf to type-1 nudges: 0.64. Type-1 cells blind to the poke: also 0.64.
- Switching off the ring's hold-back signal to type-1 cells: 0.81, unchanged. It is unused.
- Closing the horseshoe's gap by making the one type-1 cell that touches both ends a ring cell: 0.81, unchanged.
- The 4 exported trials come from export's pool (seed 0, held-out): indices 6, 10, 2 and 0, poked from 75, -15, 165 and -105 degrees. They score 0.96, 0.81, 0.93 and 0.81, and 0.00 with messages off.
